title: Dexterous Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models
description:
*Note:* We are looking for students who can start this summer and who will stay with the lab long term. The candidate will be leading this project in a first-author capacity, with support (both implementation and advisory) from members of the lab.

**Project Description**
We have been developing VLA models that are capable of cross-embodiment transfer; the models are trained on a large dataset of robot demonstrations and can be deployed on unseen embodiments, including dexterous humanoid hands. For relevant background, please review our prior work ([Cloak](https://tml.stanford.edu/cloak/)). However, these models are only capable of simple pick-and-place actions that mimic a gripper, and do not leverage the full capabilities of the dexterous hand. In this project, we will train RL policies to control the dexterous hand. The RL policies will condition on an output signal from the VLA (e.g. arm and gripper action/affordance) and use it to perform more dexterous manipulation actions. Doing so will yield a “dexterous VLA”.

**Expected Successful Outcome**
- First author publication in a top robotics/AI conference (e.g. ICRA, RSS, CoRL).
- Gain extensive experience training and deploying VLA and RL policies.
- Opportunity to continue working in the lab.

**Ideal Candidates**
- Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, for long hours, with high initiative.
- Able to dedicate a significant amount of hours (20+) each week to the project.
- Experience with deep RL and physics simulators (e.g. IsaacLab, Mujoco).
